correctness.rationale: For deterministic real coordinate steps on one row A=(1,...,1), b>=2, y≠0, iid uniform coordinate picks, residual r_k=y∏_{j<k}(1−eta_j) is deterministic. Writing effective weights w_k=eta_k∏_{j<k}(1−eta_j), W=Σw_k, independence gives risk/y²=(1−W)²/b+((b−1)/b)Σw_k² exactly. Cauchy–Schwarz minimizes Σw² at fixed W by equal weights and a strictly convex scalar quadratic fixes W=N/(N+b−1). The uniquely realized schedule eta_k=1/(N+b−1−k) has nonzero residual y(b−1)/(N+b−1) and risk y²(b−1)/(b(N+b−1)); W=1 interpolation instead costs y²(b−1)/(bN), unique equal weights. For constant 0<eta<2 geometric weights give risk floor y²(b−1)eta/(b(2−eta)) and one-step difference −y² eta(2−b eta)(1−eta)^(2N)/b, with eta=1 residual-zero exception. Independent direct rational enumeration of all coordinate index paths for (b,N)=(2,4),(3,4),(4,3), y=2 reproduced optimum risks 2/5,4/9,1/2; the algebra covers all real schedules and horizons.
